title.rendered: Declaring Who You Are In Christ | How to Declare Like Jesus Did, Day 6

excerpt.rendered: Before you declare what you want, declare who you are. Day 6 teaches believers to speak from their identity in Christ, not toward it.

content.rendered:
Before you declare what you want, declare who you are. The devil cannot defeat a believer who knows his or her identity in Christ.

The Gospel For Today | Friday, October 23, 2026 | How to Declare Like Jesus Did, Day 6

Today’s Scripture

“At that day you will know that I am in My Father, and you in Me, and I in you.”
John 14:20 (NKJV)

“Therefore, if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation; old things have passed away; behold, all things have become new.”
2 Corinthians 5:17 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

Jesus gave the Church one of its most radical sentences in John 14:20: “You in Me, and I in you.” The AMPC says, “At that time [when that day comes] you will know [for yourselves] that I am in My Father, and you [are] in Me, and I [am] in you.” The TPT renders it, “When that day comes, you will know that I am in the Father and that you are one with me, for I will be in you.” Then Paul finishes the picture in 2 Corinthians 5:17, “in Christ” is a new species; the old is gone; the new is here. “Behold, all things have become new.”

Many believers try to declare their way into an identity they already possess. From Lagos to London, from Manila to Nairobi to São Paulo, we have watched sincere Christians straining to become what the gospel says they already are. Declaration is not how we earn righteousness; it is how we agree with the righteousness Jesus has already given us. You do not declare “I am trying to be a child of God.” You declare, “I am a child of God,” because the Spirit of adoption has already said so (Romans 8:15–16).

Jesus declared His own identity on purpose. “I am the Bread of Life.” “I am the Light of the World.” “I am the Good Shepherd.” “Before Abraham was, I AM.” He did not announce what He was reaching for; He announced what He already was. And He taught His followers to do the same: “You are the salt of the earth. You are the light of the world” (Matthew 5:13–14). Identity precedes activity. Who you are determines what you can declare.

So before you ever decree a thing over your health, your home, or your harvest, settle who is doing the decreeing. In Christ you are a new creation; you are seated with Him in heavenly places; you are chosen, royal, holy, and His own possession; you are more than a conqueror. These are not slogans. They are the legal reality of your union with Jesus. Say them until you believe them. Keep saying them when the devil disagrees.

The Pattern of Declaration

Acknowledge. Scripture does not describe who you hope to be. It describes who you already are in Christ. The gospel is not aspiration; it is positional truth.

Personalise. Replace every “I feel like a failure” with “I am the righteousness of God in Christ Jesus” (2 Corinthians 5:21). Receive the identity before you rehearse it.

Proclaim. Speak in the indicative, not the subjunctive. Not “I wish I were loved,” but “I am deeply loved by God.” Not “I hope God accepts me,” but “I am accepted in the Beloved.”

Declaration

I declare and acknowledge that I am in Christ, and Christ is in me. I am a new creation; the old is gone and the new has come. I am a child of God, loved before I was born, chosen before the foundation of the world. I am righteous, redeemed, and seated with Christ in heavenly places. I am a royal priest and a holy nation. I am more than a conqueror through Him who loved me. No label the enemy gives me can override the name Jesus gives me. I live from my identity, not toward it. In Jesus’ name. Amen.
